info.title: Smart Commerce Platform
info.description:
Customer storefront and operations API for the Smart Commerce Platform.

**Money.** Amounts are whole Vietnamese đồng transported as decimal
strings (`"45000"`), because JSON numbers cannot hold a 64-bit integer
safely in every client. Never parse them into a float.

**Errors.** Every failure returns the same envelope with a stable
machine-readable `code`; branch on that, never on `message`.

**Store scope.** Admin operations require both the role permission and
an active membership of the target store. Store context comes from the
route or the host, never from a query parameter.

**Payments.** MVP settles in `CASH` or `BANK_TRANSFER` only. A generated
VietQR is not a confirmation of payment: authorized staff confirm the
actual bank credit.

One member's standing and their full history, most recent first

get.description:
A store has a handful of menus, so every one is returned, inside the
designed page envelope: the shape stays the documented one even where
pagination has nothing to do.

put.description:
One request for the whole menu, because that is one decision a kitchen
makes once; sending it dish by dish would leave the shop half-prepared
whenever a tab is closed in the middle.
put.summary: The morning prep sheet: how many portions of each dish were made today

get.description:
`status_counts` comes along because the screen that reads this is a work
queue: "how many orders are waiting" has to be the real number, not the
number that happens to be on the first page. Open statuses only, which
is what the partial index covers and what a queue is about.

Master-data products, including drafts and archived ones

get.description:
The content type is pinned to what the file was accepted as and
`nosniff` forbids the browser from deciding otherwise, so a file can
never be interpreted as anything but that image type. Both route
parameters are constrained to a UUID shape, which leaves no way to
express a path at all, let alone one that climbs out of the directory.

post.summary: Idempotent: calling it twice, or with a session already gone, is not an error

LoginRequest.description:
Validates the designed `LoginRequest`.

The password is never logged or echoed: bootstrap/app.php already lists it
among the fields excluded from flashed input.

password.description:
Minimum length is a rule for CHOOSING a password, not for typing
one: enforcing it here would tell an attacker which guesses are
too short to be real.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

price.description: The store price, which overrides the variant default.

modifier_groups.description: Modifiers are designed but not built in this milestone.

Designed, not built in this milestone. An empty array is the
truthful answer: this product carries no modifier groups.

RedeemRewardRequest.description: Spends a member's points on a reward, recorded against the staff member who did it.
RedeemRewardRequest.title: RedeemRewardRequest

ReplaceMenuRequest.description:
Validates `UpdateMenuRequest`: a full replacement of a menu.

The portion limits match the admin form's
(`apps/admin-web/src/lib/product-form.ts`), and the price rule is the same
digits-only string rule the catalog uses - one definition of "a price", not
two that can drift (CLAUDE.md section 6).

modifier_price_overrides.description:
Designed, not built. Silently dropping overrides would leave the
caller believing a price it never saved.

schedules.description:
Schedules and date exceptions are designed but not stored yet.
Accepting them would promise a menu window that nothing enforces.

ReplaceMenuRequest.title: ReplaceMenuRequest

SaveCouponRequest.description:
Validates a coupon, for both create and edit.

Shape only. Whether the numbers make sense together - a percentage inside
1..100, a fixed amount no bigger than the order it requires, a ceiling only
on a percentage - is the domain's answer, because a seeder and a future
import have to be held to the same rules (CLAUDE.md section 3).

`redeemed_count` is deliberately not accepted: how many times a code has
been used is the system's record, not a form field.

discount_value.description:
A percentage or an amount, decided by discount_type; the domain
judges the pair.

usage_limit_per_customer.description:
Designed for later: a limit per customer needs an identity to
count against, and guest checkout has no answer to that yet
(CLAUDE.md section 15). Accepting it would promise a rule
nothing enforces.

SaveCouponRequest.title: SaveCouponRequest

SaveProductRequest.description:
Validates the `ProductRequest` payload for both create and update.

One class for both, because the designed contract has one request schema for
both and a rule that holds on create but not on update is not a rule.

These limits deliberately mirror the client-side rules in
`apps/admin-web/src/lib/product-form.ts`. The client's copy exists to give
immediate feedback in the form; this one is the rule, because the server is
the only party that cannot be bypassed (CLAUDE.md section 6).

image_url.description:
A photo from the upload endpoint, echoed back unchanged. Checked
against the shape this API issues so a product cannot be made to
point at someone else's host, which would turn a menu into a
beacon for whoever owns it.

category_id.description:
Two ways to say which category, and sending both is a 422 rather
than a guess. The pair is checked again in the application layer,
which is where the rule belongs for non-HTTP callers.

base_price_amount.description:
Digits only, as a string. A JSON number cannot carry 64-bit dong
safely, and the digits-only pattern is what rejects a negative
price, "1e3" and "12.50" in one rule (CLAUDE.md section 6).

modifier_group_ids.description:
Designed, not built. Accepting and discarding them would be worse
than refusing: the caller would believe the modifiers were saved.

SaveProductRequest.title: SaveProductRequest

SaveRewardRequest.description:
Validates a reward, for both create and edit.

Shape only, same split `SaveProductRequest` draws for its own icon field:
the actual icon catalogue is the admin UI's concern, not a list this
endpoint has to keep in sync with it.
SaveRewardRequest.title: SaveRewardRequest

SetDailyPortionsRequest.description:
Validates the morning prep sheet.

One line per dish, and the same dish twice is refused rather than resolved:
a sheet that says both forty and sixty bánh mì has no correct answer, and
picking the last one silently would be a guess about someone's morning.
SetDailyPortionsRequest.title: SetDailyPortionsRequest

TransitionOrderRequest.description:
Validates `TransitionOrderRequest`: where this order is going, and why.

The target status is explicit rather than a "next" command. Two staff
members tapping at once would both mean something different by "next", and
the second tap would move the order one step further than anyone intended.
Sending the status the operator saw turns that race into a 409 they can see
(CLAUDE.md section 6).

Whether the move is legal at all is the state machine's answer, not this
one. A Form Request can only say the field is a known status.
TransitionOrderRequest.title: TransitionOrderRequest

UpdateLoyaltySettingsRequest.description: Changes how many points a PAID order earns, and the loyal-tier threshold.
UpdateLoyaltySettingsRequest.title: UpdateLoyaltySettingsRequest

UpdateMenuItemAvailabilityRequest.description:
Validates `UpdateMenuItemAvailabilityRequest`.

The sold-out switch is required; the portion counts are optional, and
"omitted" is kept distinct from "set to null" so flipping the switch cannot
wipe the kitchen's numbers.
UpdateMenuItemAvailabilityRequest.title: UpdateMenuItemAvailabilityRequest

UploadProductImageRequest.description:
Validates one uploaded product photo.

These rules are the cheap first pass. They read what the client declared, so
the authoritative check is the content sniff in UploadProductImage, which
reads the bytes: a rule on the declared type can be satisfied by renaming a
file.
UploadProductImageRequest.title: UploadProductImageRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
